title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & response formatting
author: Ava Patel
description:
Motivation: bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer closer to OpenAI semantics for a broader set of customer workloads (streaming, tool/function calling, structured output). This change set focuses on: 1) supporting additional params (logprobs, echo, best_of passthrough where applicable), 2) strict roles handling and role normalization between assistant/system/user, 3) stop sequence semantics parity, 4) streaming stability when combined with function/tool call events and structured output formatting, and 5) response formatting hooks so downstream SDKs receive OpenAI-shaped payloads.

Scope and summary: single PR that touches api gateway, compatibility shim, streaming SSE path, and tests/e2e harness. This is a backward-compatible behavior change for the OpenAI compatibility endpoint; feature toggles are used where runtime risk exists.

Checklist:
- [x] Add support for passthrough of logprobs and best_of when the runtime supports deterministic reranking
- [x] Normalize message roles (system/user/assistant) and reject invalid role values with 400
- [x] Implement stop sequence handling consistent with OpenAI: array and string forms, prioritized early stopping, and interaction with streaming chunks
- [x] Stabilize SSE streaming: ensure flush ordering, idempotent reconnection handling, and proper function call event boundaries
- [x] Format structured outputs (tools/functions) into content and delta messages that match OpenAI's streaming shape
- [x] Add integration tests and augment existing chat parity test matrix
- [x] Update docs + release notes

Notes: Because some model runtimes rely on token-level approximations for logprobs, we pass logprobs through only when the runtime advertises token-logprob support. For older runtimes we return null to match OpenAI behavior. Stop semantics are implemented in the runtime and surfaced by the compat layer to avoid double-truncation. Streaming fixes focus on two classes of bugs observed in canaries: (1) partial function call payloads arriving out-of-order across batches, (2) SSE reconnects duplicating deltas. We add an SSE dedupe id and ensure final function call 'end' events are atomic.

Related: ENG-1423 (chat parity roadmap), ENG-1478 (streaming canary failures), small follow-ups will be opened for SDK-specific helpers.
